Analysis: Both hypotheses explore novel roles for RMDN1 in modulating epigenetic landscapes in liver neoplasms. Hypothesis 1 proposes a mechanism by which upregulation of RMDN1 recruits HDAC1 and other co‐repressors to establish a repressive chromatin state, shifting HDAC1 from an oncogenic factor to a tumor suppressor. This model is relatively simpler, with clearly defined testable outcomes (via ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, CRISPR screens) and an arguably more plausible direct causal role. Hypothesis 2, while innovative in suggesting a dual, context-dependent scaffold function for RMDN1 that toggles between repressive and activating complexes, introduces more complexity that may hinder clear testing and mechanistic elucidation. Both approaches employ cutting-edge techniques, but Hypothesis 1 exhibits greater clarity in its proposed mechanism and is more straightforward to validate experimentally, with comparable safety considerations.
